headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors: AutoGPT’s filesystem/CLI outputs can be consumed by gpt-engineer’s write-and-run workflow, creating unsafe default interaction paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read/write files and call APIs, while gpt-engineer reads a user project directory and writes files before offering to run them. That shared filesystem bridge makes instruction-like content in AutoGPT outputs plausible input to gpt-engineer, though no MCP or clipboard bridge is documented. The pathway exists in default workflows, but not as a proven raw-web parser hijack.
conditions: IF AutoGPT writes attacker-controlled instructions into the shared project directory AND gpt-engineer ingests that file as prompt context, injection is possible.
IF the two agents are connected only by manual copy-paste, the risk drops to low.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories.
Strip instructions from files before gpt-engineer reads them.
Use a human review step for any AutoGPT-generated text.
Disable automatic ingestion of arbitrary project files where possible.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for agent-generated files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress; gpt-engineer reads and writes a project directory and can send prompts to a configured model. If sensitive files land in the shared workspace, both agents can expose them through model calls or generated outputs. The profiles do not show PHI or secrets handling beyond OPENAI_API_KEY, so this is a workspace leakage risk rather than a confirmed regulated-data breach.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the shared project directory, both agents can read them.
IF either agent forwards file contents into model prompts, those contents may leave the local workspace.
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of the shared project directory.
Use separate workspaces per agent.
Redact secrets before either agent runs.
Restrict outbound model access to non-sensitive projects.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on file ingestion.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, and gpt-engineer can execute shell commands, install packages, write files, and uses shared project-directory state across instances. Even though gpt-engineer does not modify git state, both agents can mutate the same workspace concurrently, so default coordination is unsafe and can overwrite or corrupt work products.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory, concurrent writes can collide.
IF AutoGPT and gpt-engineer are run in parallel, file overwrites or partial edits can occur.
mitigations: Run only one agent per project directory at a time.
Use per-agent branches or copies of the workspace.
Pause one agent before the other writes files.
Add a manual diff review before merging outputs.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional workspace coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer is explicitly a write-then-offer-to-run workflow, so if it consumes AutoGPT output as authoritative, errors can cascade into generated code and execution with user privileges. AutoGPT can emit unverified plans or code-like text, and gpt-engineer can turn that into files and runnable artifacts. This is a default dangerous pathway, not just a niche misconfiguration.
conditions: IF gpt-engineer treats AutoGPT output as authoritative without verification, incorrect instructions can become code.
IF the generated code is then run, downstream effects can include arbitrary shell execution under the user's privileges.
mitigations: Require human verification of AutoGPT outputs before use.
Do not auto-run generated code.
Compare generated files against the original prompt and expected behavior.
Limit execution to disposable environments.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before file generation and execution.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data class is explicitly identified for either agent, and both profiles are open-source with docs-only evidence. The main compliance concern is operational: gpt-engineer handles OPENAI_API_KEY and can write generated source code, while AutoGPT has filesystem and network access. Without a stated residency or retention mismatch, this is a documented-gap risk rather than a clear breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into the shared workspace, compliance review is required.
IF deployment policy forbids sending project contents to third-party model APIs, the current setup may violate policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Review retention settings for the configured model provider.
Document which files may be sent to external APIs.
Use a separate environment for sensitive projects.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency and retention.
